title: Functional accuracy to conversation blocking
original_endpoint: HateCheck’s constructed English functional hate-speech cases under the retained hate policy.
source_result: The manuscript describes tests of 29 linguistic functions; its representative evidence table reports 3,728 cases.
valid_bounded_use: Diagnosis of the represented linguistic functions.
target_claim: The functional-suite results justify automatically blocking English conversations under the same hate policy.
limitations: The suite is not an estimate of deployment prevalence.
The deliberately extended claim is the survey’s worked example, not a claim attributed to the HateCheck authors.
transport_test: Pair artifact and session observations on an independently adjudicated conversation sample, retaining benign-sensitive controls and measuring threshold-specific errors.
supported_claim: The suite can diagnose the linguistic functions it represents.
suggested_controls: Benign-sensitive conversations under the same policy.

S.reason: The hypothetical claim explicitly holds the hate policy fixed.

C.reason: Conversational history is outside the functional artifact tests.

O.reason: Session adjudication is not established by artifact-level functional cases.

P.reason: The constructed test distribution does not establish deployed conversation traffic performance.

E.reason: Threshold-specific blocking errors and consequences are not validated.

title: Refusal detection to justified refusal
original_endpoint: WildGuard’s separate prompt-harmfulness, response-harmfulness, and refusal-detection labels.
source_result: The source study distinguishes these tasks; refusal-detection F1 measures identification of a refusal.
valid_bounded_use: Identifying refusals and evaluating the separately defined task labels on the tested exchanges.
target_claim: Refusal-detection F1 alone establishes justified blocking on the same exchanges.
limitations: A refusal can still leak harmful information.
A safe response need not refuse.
This is an illustrative extended claim, not the WildGuard authors’ wording.
transport_test: Jointly assess the request’s policy status, response content, permitted safe alternatives, and intervention consequences. A new threshold on refusal occurrence is insufficient.
supported_claim: Refusal-detection performance supports the refusal-occurrence task under the tested conditions.
suggested_controls: Harmful requests and benign-sensitive requests, including safe non-refusal answers.

S.reason: Policy is fixed in the hypothetical extension.

C.reason: Input access and exchanges are fixed.

O.reason: A refusal-occurrence label does not establish refusal appropriateness.

E.reason: A blocking rule requires consequences and policy-grounded appropriateness, not refusal detection alone.

title: One output to repeated-access exposure
original_endpoint: A hypothetical image-level failure rate under a fixed policy and interface.
source_result: For fixed independent trials at a given prompt and configuration, repeated-access risk is analytically 1 − (1 − r)^n; the worked claim uses n = 100.
valid_bounded_use: An image-level rate describes its stated single-output event. The analytic conversion applies only under the stated fixed-independent-trial assumptions.
target_claim: The same image-level failure rate estimates harm within 100 attempts, with policy and interface fixed and no enforcement action specified.
limitations: The case is hypothetical and is not an empirical audit of a named paper.
The equation does not cover dependent or adaptive attempts without additional analysis.
Averaging prompt-specific rates before the nonlinear conversion need not equal averaging their repeated-access risks.
transport_test: Measure prompt-level repeats with a declared stopping rule and quantify uncertainty at the prompt or session level; use the analytic conversion only for fixed independent trials.
supported_claim: The source rate concerns its specified image-level event.
suggested_controls: Maintain a consistent policy and adjudication protocol across one-output and repeated-access measurements.

S.reason: The hypothetical claim holds policy fixed.

O.reason: One-image failure and at least one failure within 100 attempts are different events.

P.reason: Repeated access changes the probability regime; correlated or adaptive attempts require a distinct analysis.

E.reason: No action is specified in this hypothetical claim. N does not mean demonstrated absence of evidence for a named action.

title: Static screening to component release
original_endpoint: Concept QuickLook’s original NSFW categories in static single-file embedding inspection; no toxicity crosswalk is established by this case.
source_result: The manuscript describes SD 1.5/2.0 embedding inspection over 800 reviewed files (500 downloaded and 300 customized), with 15% marked NSFW. These numbers do not establish ecosystem prevalence.
valid_bounded_use: Configuration-bound static concept inspection can prioritize further investigation; it does not validate automatic release.
target_claim: Single-file embedding inspection justifies automatic release across arbitrary compatible compositions while retaining the original NSFW categories.
action: Automatically release components across arbitrary compatible compositions.
limitations: The reported Accuracy/FPR/FNR values are not jointly reconcilable under conventional binary definitions.
The metric inconsistency concerns evidence quality separately from coordinate support.
Several survey authors also authored Concept QuickLook.
The NSFW policy must not be silently relabeled targeted social harm or a general toxicity rate.
transport_test: Test both scanner-selected and scanner-cleared files on declared bases, scales, triggers, and seeds, with independent image adjudication and benign controls; reconcile the original metric definitions.
supported_claim: The static inspection feasibility result is bound to its original endpoint and tested configuration.
suggested_controls: Benign controls and behavioral audits of both scanner-selected and scanner-cleared components.

S.reason: D retains the source NSFW endpoint; it does not establish a mapping to targeted social harm.

C.reason: Executed paths and arbitrary compatible compositions are not covered by a static single-file screen.

O.reason: Static similarity does not observe generated outcomes after loading.

P.reason: The distribution of compositions, bases, triggers, scales, and seeds is untested by static similarity.

E.reason: Release costs and an operational release rule are not validated.
